launches.tagline: Computer-use agents that work cross-border transaction alert investigations end to end: collect evidence, produce an assessment, draft an RFI.
launches.body:
We're building Zomma: AI operations employees for finance back offices, starting with cross-border transaction alert investigations.

**TL;DR:** Zomma agents work directly inside the software your ops team already uses. No APIs, no integrations. For every cross-border alert, the agent gathers the evidence, writes the draft assessment, and drafts the RFI, end-to-end. Running live compliance-ops pilots with a US RIA and a $10B AUM wealth tech. 92% on OSWorld.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDXDKH_tYhg>

## **The problem**

Cross-border payments trip more monitoring rules than anything else in the queue: sanctions name hits on foreign counterparties, high-risk corridors, first-time beneficiaries. Most alerts are false positives (McKinsey: over 90% in transaction monitoring), but every one still needs to be investigated. 20 to 60 minutes per case, across five or six systems, several with no API at all. And the evidence that clears them sits in foreign company registries and local-language adverse media. 

So review capacity scales the only way it can: hiring. When hiring lags volume, alerts pile into backlogs that take months to clear, and backlogs are what regulators fine: $3.8B in AML penalties last year alone.

## **What Zomma does**

Zomma agents work the queue on the same screens your analysts use: case manager, screening tool, admin panel, inbox, web search. Onboarding looks like hiring: an SOP and a login.

On a transaction monitoring alert, the agent

* pulls the KYC profile and payment history
* verifies the invoice and researches the counterparty, including registries you can only search by hand
* writes a case-specific assessment with every claim cited to the source screen
* drafts the RFI when documents are missing

Every step is logged and replayable: timestamped screenshots of every page checked, numbered citations, explicit no-match statements, a screen-by-screen trail an examiner can follow.

## **Why start with cross-border alerts**

If an employee can do it on a screen, Zomma can learn it: the rest of the compliance queue, payment disputes, client onboarding, trade ops. Cross-border alerts come first because they have the exact shape our agents are best at: high-volume, parallelizable work that needs real reasoning but follows a defined workflow to a documented disposition. They're also the hardest cases to automate any other way: the evidence lives in registries and portals that will never have APIs. And agents scale with the queue: a volume spike means provisioning two more that afternoon; a BPO batch takes a month to train.

Computer-use agents only recently got accurate enough to trust with a live queue, which is why we're building this now. Our state-of-the-art computer-use harness with our procedural and workflow memory system scores 92% on OSWorld.

## **Team**

* **Jihyun (CEO):** founding team at a Blackstone-backed hedge fund, scaled Asia's largest wealth tech, Goldman engineer.
* **Cash (CTO):** backend systems behind $20B+ in yearly transactions, trains VLMs for computer use.
* **Varun (CPO):** high-performance infra at Apple, design-verification agents at Bronco AI (YC S23).

Send us \~100 closed cross-border alerts and we'll show you what the agent would have done with them, or book a call: zommalabs.com/call.

launches.tagline: Full-stack AI debt collection company
launches.body:
A letter arrives in the mail.

Impossible to understand.

Another one.

Then the phone calls start.

Once a day. Unpleasant, sometimes hostile.

This is how debt collection works in 2026.

**We’re here to fix it.**\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X9mVp2ZyJMUhCcHN6NadzMNLV5S63Wpv](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X9mVp2ZyJMUhCcHN6NadzMNLV5S63Wpv/view?usp=sharing)

# TL;DR

Audun is an AI-native debt collection company. Our agents automate the collections process end to end, from reminders and negotiations to back-office and legal work. This reduces collection costs for creditors, and enables humans to spend their time on the conversations that matter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111293&key=user_uploads/3587634/839f47e4-cdd7-45ed-befd-c621930fef65)

# Ask

We’re looking for introductions to collection leaders at banks, lenders, utilities, telcos, and other high-volume creditors.

# The problem

The debt collection industry is broken. It runs on call centers, paper letters, and software built in the 90s. While the rest of the world is preparing for AGI, the topic of the industry is still email and cloud.

All these inefficiencies ultimately end up with the consumer: incomprehensible letters arriving by snail mail, hostile phone calls, and fees stacking up on a bill they may never have seen. They're paying the cost of an archaic system.

# The solution

Audun is an AI-native debt collection company. We automate up to 90% of cases across the whole business, from front to back office. Our agents manage reminders, negotiations, payment plans, and settlements across voice, SMS, email, and WhatsApp. They operate within creditor-defined rules, log every action, and escalate sensitive cases to humans with the full context attached. Behind the scenes, they handle tasks such as skip tracing, payment verification, and legal document drafting.

By automating the grunt work of collections, Audun lowers collection costs for creditors and, ultimately, borrowing costs for consumers. We enable people to focus on the conversations that matter, where human judgment is still required, giving customers the treatment they deserve.

We started out in the Nordics, which has some of the strictest collections regulation in the world. Compliance is critical in this industry, so we built our agents to handle the toughest version of it first. 

# Who we are

We’re four founders with experience across McKinsey, Midjourney, and Norway’s first unicorn. We’ve seen firsthand how manual this industry is, and how stuck the incumbents are. We decided to build the company this industry needs from the ground up.

name: Definite
long_description:
Definite is where finance teams build everyday back-office agents on one live model of their books. We plug into your ERP, ledger, payroll, and payments read-only and compile everything into one clean model that stays current as money moves. Your back-office team then builds agents on top in plain English. We never write back and we never move money. The agents are yours, the plumbing is ours.

We met in first year computer science at Waterloo and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo. At Optiver they ran an n8n hackathon and the interns automated basically nothing. It couldn't talk to the systems that mattered. When we pitched banks and fintechs on agents, they kept telling us the same thing. The agent isn't the hard part, getting clean data out of their systems is.

Right now, automating anything in a back office means engineers hand-stitching data from a dozen sources in different formats on different schedules. Tools like n8n and Workato assume your data is already clean and joined. In finance it never is. So the teams with the most repetitive work and smallest budgets get nothing.

The hard part is the compiler. Every source gets cleaned, matched, and joined into one live model of transactions, invoices, vendors, and payments, and it has to stay right as money lands every day. 

Everyone throws engineers at this. We're doing it once so nobody has to again. Every back office is getting agents eventually. Whoever owns the data they read from owns the thing all of them depend on, and eventually the books themselves. That's what we're building.

launches.body:
_AI agents that run the entire regulatory reporting pipeline for banks, from raw ledger data to the filed report._

**_TL;DR_**_: Definite automates regulatory reporting for banks end to end, from raw ledger data to filed report, turning weeks of manual work into hours._ [usedefinite.com](http://usedefinite.com)

Hey! We're Gurshabd, Mazin and Farhan from Definite.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ji1ae8y_V4E>

**The Problem**

Proving to regulators that their books follow the rules is a constant, non-negotiable obligation for banks. Each report is thousands of numbers, personally signed off by an executive. Getting it wrong can mean a **fine up to a million dollars** over a single undetected error. Producing that proof is slow, and doesn't even guarantee it's correct. 

Here's where the current system breaks down:

1. **Wasted Hours:** A controller pulls data from the core system into Excel and maps it line by line by hand. By regulators' own estimate, one quarterly filing takes weeks of employee time, time pulled from higher-value finance work every quarter.
2. **False Confidence:** The software banks use to file checks formatting, not truth. A loan mapped to the wrong schedule line sails through every check. Nothing catches it until an examiner does, and by then it's not a mistake, it's a violation.

**The Solution**

**Report agents:** We connect to your books and our agents build the reports you owe.

**Verification engine:** Every number is recomputed from source records and checked against a versioned rulebook, so each line carries its rule and source data.

**Self-correcting agents:** When a check fails, the agent gets the reason and fixes it in seconds. Real exceptions come to your team with a drafted explanation, not a blank error. This loop is why our agents are the most accurate in finance.

**Receipts:** Every check produces a tamper-evident receipt you can hand an examiner or auditor.

Your team reviews and signs instead of building.

**How we got here**

Gurshabd worked at BitGo, a regulated crypto custodian, where attestations proving customer assets matched the ledger were built by hand every period. Farhan worked at Meta where he delved extensively into machine learning and building AI agents. Mazin saw Optiver recheck daily regulatory numbers by hand, then built LLM agents at [Boosted.ai](http://Boosted.ai) and learned finance people won't act on AI output unless every number comes with its source.

The lesson from all three: in finance, producing a number is cheap, proving it is the job. On two public reporting benchmarks, DeepSeek V3 with our verification engine outperformed GPT-5 on reconciliation accuracy (FinBalance) at roughly 50× lower cost, and beat the entire published field on XBRL calculation validation (FinAuditing).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105798&key=user_uploads/2947446/1b80714c-9a38-4d02-a037-ab05ad2c9205)

You’ve heard of so many AI accounting startups already. These new “AI-native” accounting firms are still designed to be run by humans in two facets: the first 25%, fostering client relationships, and the final 25%, signing off and filing with the IRS.

* Analyzes new deals and drafts the investment memos
* Monitors the portfolio, marks valuations, and answers questions in Slack ("what's our exposure to X?")
* Produces and checks compliance certificates, and handles covenant and LP reporting

Why it works when nothing else has:

* **It's AI-native, not a rules engine.** Older tools only work if you hand-code every rule, so they break on messy, real-world data. Levocred's agents read your actual documents and tapes and reason across them. We already run consumer, fintech, litigation finance, and MCA through the same engine.
* **You stay in control** with full auditability and no waiting on a vendor's engineers
* **It compounds.** Every document you load makes it smarter about your book. That data moat is yours. It’s why usage only grows.

The result: a draw that took a day of Excel takes minutes, monitoring runs continuously instead of monthly, and your team spends its time on judgment, not grunt work.
